- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates early in a downward trend (especially after sentiment shifts to bearish); adjust downward by 1–4% for first 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% for next 2–4 days.  
- When sentiment is mixed or trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–3% downward correction if price is above 30-day moving average.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day high, reduce by 5–10% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- If sentiment is bullish but price is falling, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 2–4 days.
